Paying for Air

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
: Residents of the City of Joburg have for years battled crippling water outages… now, we can show that some residents are - quite literally - paying for air when the water isn’t running.

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche’s subs are flooded with residents battling to live
with Joburg Water’s "water-shifting" - the equivalent of load-shedding for water.
Water interruptions occur almost daily for many residents/areas.
The crux: residents are paying for air. Why? How much? Who/What is to blame?
The significance: what air in the pipes say about Joburg’s water future.

Summary:
A-STORYLINE: I want to take our presenter with Ravin Singh to several
Johannesburg suburbs (Melville, Kensington, Coronationville) to show how this
overcharging is still happening.
By the end of last year residents got so fed up with the outages that they formed a
Water Crisis Committee to escalate the problem and demand solutions from the City
of Joburg - which is in disarray.
Ravin is a founding member of that Committee - we go with him to visit selected
residents' homes to show what’s happened with their metres and their billing. He’s a
great speaker - the group nominated him.
Ravin tells us how residents have kept videos over a period that show how their
water is off (showing taps not running), and then showing how their water metres
continue to run, and therefore bill them.
Our big fight in the story will be with Joburg Water – and we will try to confront the
City about the billing.
It’s a scam on a municipal scale.
SCOPE OF THE PROBLEM: Some more examples of people willing to be
interviewed in their yards:
● Louise Grenfell, Melville: “During all the months when water has been
turned off overnight, our bill has consistently increased, whilst we are using a
minimum amount of water. I did report it some months ago, but was told to
check the meter. The meter reading was correct, but the amount of water
used was incorrect. The bill increases every month, whilst we are using less
and less water.”
● Basetsana Esther Meletse, Westrand: Incorrect high water consumption
due to air in meter
● Rahima Shaik, Kensington: Meters are not read regularly then they guess
readings and eventually you get a huge bill. Also when water has been shut
air pressure causes higher readings.
● Anja Middleton, Johannesburg: Astronomical bills for no water and water
cuts are unbelievable. Water comes in through the meter we get charged for
it. Then when there's a cut it all just flows right back .... we are paying for
water not used and water paid for twice.    
● Joshua Myles, Coronationville: When supply returns the air flowing through
the meter gives you an unrealistic consumption/usage. It's a sin to see the
elderly residents having to run after the water tankers trying to get
water.


Further information:
SO WHAT ARE WE SAYING IN THIS STORY:
B STORYLINE: On one level it’s a scam perpetrated by a dysfunctional municipality.
But the air in the pipes is a symptom of a very big conundrum: the fact that there’s
more demand for water than supply in the system.
Rand Water gets its water from the Vaal System, purifies it and feeds it on to
Johannesburg Water which distributes to reservoirs and water towers for the City of
Johannesburg - which levies a charge to residents for providing them with water.
The planning for JHB’s future hinges on the Lesotho Highlands Water Project - it’s
critical Phase 2 was meant to be concluded by 2019.
However, it only started last year - Water and Sanitation Minister Senzo Mchunu
says the new estimated completion date is 2027!

DEEP BACKGROUND:
The Integrated Vaal River System is fed with water from the Lesotho’s Highland
Water Scheme - and Joburg Water manages the reservoirs and water towers they
need to keep pressure at certain levels.
It’s increasingly clear there isn’t enough water for all of Jozi, especially in summer. To
balance the pressure in the system Joburg Water applies watershifting - often at
night, when they switch off the water supply to specific areas. This means residents
don’t have water for hours, while others in higher-lying areas don't have water for
days because of THAT constant lack of pressure.
Joburg Water is not fixing enough of the water leaks that you still see popping out all
over town despite many initiatives that we’ve reported on. City of Johannesburg
doesn't give Joburg Water enough money to fix the leaks; the repairs are poorly
done - numerous potholes around town are caused by these leaks and how badly
they have been repaired.
The Water Crises Committee went to several civil society organizations about their
water bills, water outages and unattended leaks - Kirsten Pearson from Corruption
Watch has compiled these complaints: for example she has 85 complaints about the
air issue from all around Johannesburg, and more from across the country. They’re
consulting experts about what it means in the long run. Kirsten will bring together the
depth/scope of the problem and highlight the legal problem with it.

Script:



In the city of Joburg: water has become a real concern…
…soaring utility bills…
while leaks flood the streets:
A painful contradiction - as there’s often no water at home…
Shaheen: I was in complete shock, I have got a Bill for hundred and sixty five thousand
Inexplicable billing.
Sevena: Just to survive, we've had to gather water rainwater from the gutters
Crippling outages.
Dwayne: We went 52 days without water
Joburgers have long inundated our inbox with their complaints - the latest video evidence of interruptions and leaks come from every corner of the metro.
VIEWER VIDEOS
Now, it seems, this devastating situation is only part of what’s going wrong with the city’s water.

LINK: “Despite dealing with the leaks and outages…plot twist, Joburg residents are saying they’re literally paying for air.”
Water takes a long journey to reach every tap: From the Vaal Dam it’s pumped and made drinkable by Rand Water, who hands it on to the municipal company “Johannesburg Water” to distribute to homes.
Households have metres so that the City can bill for what’s been used.
So why are the users… so often without water?

LINK: IT IS BECOMING INCREASINGLY CLEAR THAT THERE IS NOT ENOUGH WATER FOR THE JOBURG RESIDENTS OF JOHANNESBURG, ESPECIALLY IN SUMMER, SO JOBURG WATER APPLIES WATER SHIFTING, WHERE IT SWITCHES WATER SUPPLY TO CERTAIN AREAS.
For years, water shifting seemed to hit the metro’s Southern Suburbs the hardest.
Last year Linmeyer suburb had two months of outages - Dayne Smith struggled…along with all his neighbours.
Dayne: We went 52 days without water and we had water tankers that were coming up and down providing water. It was ridiculously difficult for the elderly people it was hard. There was no guarantee as to when we would get water back
Protests erupted … (show protest action video)
breathe
Dayne’s community formed a Water Crisis Committee to escalate the issue to the national Department of Water and Sanitation.
Videos of residents protesting and council meetings.
SEGUE TO NEW SUBURB
Breathe
But now it appears that the outages were not the end of their crisis: With sudden pressure changes in the pipes every time water is switched back on, leaks sprung everywhere.
And it's through leaks … like this one… that air enters the piping system.
Breathe…
11. Despite the two-month outage, Dayne’s water bill spiked.. his meter… wildly spinning.

Dayne: Because there was no water in the pipes, air that was pushing through into our water meters and turning our water meters extremely quickly and extremely fast.
FOOTAGE OF WATER METRE TICKING OVER FROM CELL PHONE
Dayne: I'd love to go to Minister Mchunu and give him an empty water bottle and say to him please can you give me 20 rand for this empty water bottle he'd probably look at me and laugh but that's a reality that that's what we're paying for we're paying for air.
Dayne interview: Claire: if you didn't have water did your water Bill go down?
The water Bill was astronomically high.
12. While Linmeyer’s outage has SINCE been resolved, residents kept sending civil organisations Corruption Watch and WaterCan new complaints.

13. Turns out households may have been paying for air for some time… but constant water shifting made the problem more evident. Watercan executive manager Dr Ferrial Adam.

DR ADAM: We've heard people talk about air billing so we have over 80 residents in Johannesburg and over about you know forty nationally that are saying that they've had this experience.

14. There are methods for getting air out of the pipe system after outages, but Dr Adam says the city is not using them.

Dr Adam: They need to bleed the system so they usually open like a fire hydrant close by to allow the air to get out of the system and if you’re skilled you know how to do this but what we have been told is this is not happening.

BREATHE

15. So not only are residents expected to foot the bill for air…some bills have gone out of all proportion.
Take the case of Shaheen Onia in the central suburb Crosby, whose invoice skyrocketed from R3,000 to a jaw-dropping R165,000 in a month.

Shaheen: I was in complete shock, I have got a Bill for hundred and sixty five thousand which shows that I had used 2.1 million litres of water.

16. With South Africans using on average 235 liters daily, millions are highly implausible.

Shaheen: When I came outside, my water meter was sitting at 7.6 million.

17. Three months later in January, Shaheen’s bill reached nearly R300,000… it’s yet to be resolved.
Claire: What did they tell you could be the reason of why your water Bill was astronomically high
Shaheen: The only reason they gave me is a water leak and when I did call C O J they came out and had a look at the meter and they concluded that there isn't a water leak.
Finally, City of Joburg suggested he replace his metre.
LINK: “Naturally water will follow gravity, so when the water is turned back on, it will start flowing to lower-lying areas, and if you live in a high-lying area…it might mean that you will have to wait a little bit longer for your water. But unfortunately, it also causes damage to infrastructure in low-lying areas where the water pressure has built up.”
18. And that means leaks like this one, up the road in Rosettenville on Cristina de Oliveira’s commute.
Cristina: This is the community swimming pool as you can see this has been leaking since um March 2023 uh towards the end of last year they decided to open to find out why it was leaking.
Claire: When water is not coming out of your taps there's still water trickling out of here?
Cristina: And we have people coming with buckets to come and collect water.
Claire: No!
Cristina: Yes
Claire: Oh goodness.
19. In the upscale central suburb of Houghton, Water expert Dr Shan Holmes guided us on a tour of maintenance backlogs.

Dr Shan: Well this one's been like this for over a month, I think it's a great example of the problem we have, where all the piping is corroded.
20. The additional pressure from air pushing through already corroded pipes accelerates their degradation.

Dr Shan: so if the system is being off there's a huge amount of air that comes into the pipe so that when it's recommissioned and the water flows through you've got to get rid of those airlocks and those airlocks get driven through the little impeller on your water meter so it can go very rapidly
21. The air pressure frequently causes the water meter to spin even faster than it would with water flowing through it.
22. Joburg Water clearly has much to answer for. Gugulethu Quma is Operations Manager.
23. Despite expert warnings about water shifting’s damage to infrastructure, Quma claims the system is protected against pressure surges - and he says air in the pipes is uncommon.
Joburg water: Gugu: I will call it maybe there's isolated incident maybe the meter itself is also fault, there must be some form of testing and Johannesburg Water and COJ specifically they have platforms now to investigate those meters

Claire: Do we have a case of many faulty meters then across JHB? Because we've got numerous complaints of people saying this, independently of one another?

Joburg water: Gugu: We cannot rule it out, because it's a new phenomenon we haven't been throttling the systems before but now we've got high demand challenges that forces us to do unconventional responses to the system.

24. Quma’s solution? If customers suspect they have a faulty water metre, document the problem and request a new one.

25. Joburg Water say they need 2 billion rands a year to renew water infrastructure - this year’s current budget will only give them R1 billion.

LINK: “Joburg water only gets half of the money they need for infrastructure renewal and maintenance and essentially that means every year we have more to fix but with less money.”

26. Years of under-budgeting have added up to a staggering R24 billion backlog in infrastructure upgrades.

Dr Shan: There doesn't seem to be a systematized plan of pipe replacements um what we see is a constant digging up um a constant uh repair job that doesn't work and that must be costing the city millions per annum just in repairs that at the end of the day don't matter.

27. So what rating - out of ten - would Quma give Johannesburg Water?

Joburg water: Gugu: Let's give ourselves at least between 7 and 8. There's millions of residents, they receive potable water on a daily basis
Claire: At least an eight? Are you sure?
Gugu: It is a fair judgement based on our system.
Claire: if I had to go to Linmeyer now and speak to those residents who didn't have water for 52 days and were chasing water trucks you would not be on the scale, I think some areas perhaps I don't wanna take you eight away from you they won't give you eight yes but in other areas people would disagree very strongly with that rating
Gugu: Eight will fit in in certain areas.
Claire: And 2 and 3 in other areas
Gugu: Let's say under 5, because it's unacceptable anyway
Claire: Agreed.

28. Water-shifting is set to continue for the foreseeable future. In an effort to plan for the influx of people to Joburg, the government secured more water from our neighbour, Lesotho, but that life-saving deal is a decade behind schedule.

LINK: “The planning for JHB’s future hinges on the Lesotho Highlands Water Project - its critical Phase 2 was supposed to be concluded by 2019. but, it only started last year - Water and Sanitation Minister Senzo Mchunu says its estimated completion date is 2027!”
29. Until then, it seems, residents of this world-class African city may have to get used to feeling more than a little dehydrated. Or, ...may have to get used to paying for air.

Because we've got numerous complaints of people saying this, independently of one another? Joburg water: Gugu: We cannot rule it out, because it's a new phenomenon we haven't been throttling the systems before but now we've got high demand challenges that forces us to do unconventional responses to the system. 24. Quma’s solution? If customers suspect they have a faulty water metre, document the problem and request a new one. 25. Joburg Water say they need 2 billion rands a year to renew water infrastructure - this year’s current budget will only give them R1 billion. LINK: “Joburg water only gets half of the money they need for infrastructure renewal and maintenance and essentially that means every year we have more to fix but with less money.” 26. Years of under-budgeting have added up to a staggering R24 billion backlog in infrastructure upgrades. Dr Shan: There doesn't seem to be a systematized plan of pipe replacements um what we see is a constant digging up um a constant uh repair job that doesn't work and that must be costing the city millions per annum just in repairs that at the end of the day don't matter. 27. So what rating - out of ten - would Quma give Johannesburg Water? Joburg water: Gugu: Let's give ourselves at least between 7 and 8. There's millions of residents, they receive potable water on a daily basis Claire: At least an eight? Are you sure? Gugu: It is a fair judgement based on our system. Claire: if I had to go to Linmeyer now and speak to those residents who didn't have water for 52 days and were chasing water trucks you would not be on the scale, I think some areas perhaps I don't wanna take you eight away from you they won't give you eight yes but in other areas people would disagree very strongly with that rating Gugu: Eight will fit in in certain areas. Claire: And 2 and 3 in other areas Gugu: Let's say under 5, because it's unacceptable anyway Claire: Agreed. 28. Water-shifting is set to continue for the foreseeable future. In an effort to plan for the influx of people to Joburg, the government secured more water from our neighbour, Lesotho, but that life-saving deal is a decade behind schedule. LINK: “The planning for JHB’s future hinges on the Lesotho Highlands Water Project - its critical Phase 2 was supposed to be concluded by 2019. but, it only started last year - Water and Sanitation Minister Senzo Mchunu says its estimated completion date is 2027!” 29. Until then, it seems, residents of this world-class African city may have to get used to feeling more than a little dehydrated. Or, ...may have to get used to paying for air.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): : Residents of the City of Joburg have for years battled crippling water outages… now, we can show that some residents are - quite literally - paying for air when the water isn’t running.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche’s subs are flooded with residents battling to live with Joburg Water’s "water-shifting" - the equivalent of load-shedding for water. Water interruptions occur almost daily for many residents/areas. The crux: residents are paying for air. Why? How much? Who/What is to blame? The significance: what air in the pipes say about Joburg’s water future.
metadata.Summary: A-STORYLINE: I want to take our presenter with Ravin Singh to several Johannesburg suburbs (Melville, Kensington, Coronationville) to show how this overcharging is still happening. By the end of last year residents got so fed up with the outages that they formed a Water Crisis Committee to escalate the problem and demand solutions from the City of Joburg - which is in disarray. Ravin is a founding member of that Committee - we go with him to visit selected residents' homes to show what’s happened with their metres and their billing. He’s a great speaker - the group nominated him. Ravin tells us how residents have kept videos over a period that show how their water is off (showing taps not running), and then showing how their water metres continue to run, and therefore bill them. Our big fight in the story will be with Joburg Water – and we will try to confront the City about the billing. It’s a scam on a municipal scale. SCOPE OF THE PROBLEM: Some more examples of people willing to be interviewed in their yards: ● Louise Grenfell, Melville: “During all the months when water has been turned off overnight, our bill has consistently increased, whilst we are using a minimum amount of water. I did report it some months ago, but was told to check the meter. The meter reading was correct, but the amount of water used was incorrect. The bill increases every month, whilst we are using less and less water.” ● Basetsana Esther Meletse, Westrand: Incorrect high water consumption due to air in meter ● Rahima Shaik, Kensington: Meters are not read regularly then they guess readings and eventually you get a huge bill. Also when water has been shut air pressure causes higher readings. ● Anja Middleton, Johannesburg: Astronomical bills for no water and water cuts are unbelievable. Water comes in through the meter we get charged for it. Then when there's a cut it all just flows right back .... we are paying for water not used and water paid for twice. ● Joshua Myles, Coronationville: When supply returns the air flowing through the meter gives you an unrealistic consumption/usage. It's a sin to see the elderly residents having to run after the water tankers trying to get water.
metadata.Further information: SO WHAT ARE WE SAYING IN THIS STORY: B STORYLINE: On one level it’s a scam perpetrated by a dysfunctional municipality. But the air in the pipes is a symptom of a very big conundrum: the fact that there’s more demand for water than supply in the system. Rand Water gets its water from the Vaal System, purifies it and feeds it on to Johannesburg Water which distributes to reservoirs and water towers for the City of Johannesburg - which levies a charge to residents for providing them with water. The planning for JHB’s future hinges on the Lesotho Highlands Water Project - it’s critical Phase 2 was meant to be concluded by 2019. However, it only started last year - Water and Sanitation Minister Senzo Mchunu says the new estimated completion date is 2027! DEEP BACKGROUND: The Integrated Vaal River System is fed with water from the Lesotho’s Highland Water Scheme - and Joburg Water manages the reservoirs and water towers they need to keep pressure at certain levels. It’s increasingly clear there isn’t enough water for all of Jozi, especially in summer. To balance the pressure in the system Joburg Water applies watershifting - often at night, when they switch off the water supply to specific areas. This means residents don’t have water for hours, while others in higher-lying areas don't have water for days because of THAT constant lack of pressure. Joburg Water is not fixing enough of the water leaks that you still see popping out all over town despite many initiatives that we’ve reported on. City of Johannesburg doesn't give Joburg Water enough money to fix the leaks; the repairs are poorly done - numerous potholes around town are caused by these leaks and how badly they have been repaired. The Water Crises Committee went to several civil society organizations about their water bills, water outages and unattended leaks - Kirsten Pearson from Corruption Watch has compiled these complaints: for example she has 85 complaints about the air issue from all around Johannesburg, and more from across the country. They’re consulting experts about what it means in the long run. Kirsten will bring together the depth/scope of the problem and highlight the legal problem with it.
